explanation: UCC § 2-315 provides that the implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose arises when the seller has reason to know the buyer’s particular purpose and that the buyer is relying on the seller’s skill or judgment to select suitable goods. Merchant status is not required, so the option tracking those two elements is best.

quotes.quote: Where the seller at the time of contracting has reason to know any particular purpose for which the goods are required and that the buyer is relying on the seller's skill or judgment to select or furnish suitable goods, there is unless excluded or modified under the next section an implied warranty that the goods shall be fit for such purpose.

explanation: Smith actively participates in the rental real estate activity, so up to $25,000 of rental losses may offset nonpassive income, subject to phaseout. Because AGI of $120,000 exceeds $100,000 by $20,000, the $25,000 allowance is reduced by 50% of that excess ($10,000), leaving $15,000 deductible; the remaining $25,000 of the $40,000 loss is suspended.

quotes.quote: The aggregate amount to which paragraph (1) applies for any taxable year shall not exceed $25,000.
the $25,000 amount under paragraph (2) shall be reduced (but not below zero) by 50 percent of the amount by which the adjusted gross income of the taxpayer for the taxable year exceeds $100,000.
any passive activity loss or any loss allowable by reason of subsection (c)(7).

explanation: Acre contributed property with a $40,000 built-in gain ($100,000 FMV less $60,000 basis), and section 704(c) requires that precontribution gain to be allocated to Acre. The sale produced $100,000 of total gain, so the first $40,000 is allocated to Acre and the remaining $60,000, representing post-contribution appreciation, is shared equally by all three partners under the equal-profit-sharing agreement.

quotes.quote: income, gain, loss, and deduction with respect to property contributed to the partnership by a partner shall be shared among the partners so as to take account of the variation between the basis of the property to the partnership and its fair market value at the time of contribution
if the partnership sells section 704(c) property and recognizes gain or loss, built-in gain or loss on the property is allocated to the contributing partner
only $5,400 of gain must be allocated to A to account for A's built-in gain. The remaining $1,000 of gain is allocated equally between A and B in accordance with the partnership agreement.

explanation: For an S corporation, Carson would include his 40% pro rata share of the corporation’s nonseparately computed income, or $160,000 (40% × $400,000). The $70,000 distribution would not separately increase gross income to the extent it does not exceed his stock basis under §1368(b), so C is correct.

quotes.quote: In determining the tax under this chapter of a shareholder for the shareholder’s taxable year in which the taxable year of the S corporation ends (or for the final taxable year of a shareholder who dies, or of a trust or estate which terminates, before the end of the corporation’s taxable year), there shall be taken into account the shareholder’s pro rata share of the corporation’s—

For purposes of this subchapter, the term “ nonseparately computed income or loss ” means gross income minus the deductions allowed to the corporation under this chapter, determined by excluding all items described in paragraph (1)(A).
The distribution shall not be included in gross income to the extent that it does not exceed the adjusted basis of the stock.

explanation: The unemployment insurance system is administered through state unemployment compensation laws, which must satisfy federal approval requirements. FUTA itself imposes the tax on employers, not employees, so B is incorrect; A and C misstate eligibility and the temporary nature of unemployment benefits.

quotes.quote: The Secretary of Labor shall make no certification for payment to any State unless he finds that the law of such State, approved by the Secretary of Labor under the Federal Unemployment Tax Act [ 26 U.S.C. 3301 et seq.], includes provision for— (1) Such methods of administration
There is hereby imposed on every employer (as defined in section 3306(a)) for each calendar year an excise tax, with respect to having individuals in his employ, equal to 6 percent of the total wages

explanation: Decker's realized gain is $500,000 minus $200,000, or $300,000. Because he is a single taxpayer who owned and used the home as his principal residence for at least two of the prior five years, §121 excludes up to $250,000, leaving $50,000 recognized. His age and purchase of a replacement home do not change this result; the old rollover provision in §1034 was repealed.

quotes.quote: Gross income shall not include gain from the sale or exchange of property if, during the 5-year period ending on the date of the sale or exchange, such property has been owned and used by the taxpayer as the taxpayer’s principal residence for periods aggregating 2 years or more.
The amount of gain excluded from gross income under subsection (a) with respect to any sale or exchange shall not exceed $250,000.

explanation: A sale of Stone's 35% interest to Taylor does not terminate Studio Partnership. Under the former 12-month rule, termination required a sale or exchange of 50% or more of total interests in partnership capital and profits, and 35% is below that threshold; under current §708(b)(1), termination occurs only if the partnership's business ceases to be carried on by any partner in a partnership.

quotes.quote: For purposes of subsection (a), a partnership shall be considered as terminated only if no part of any business, financial operation, or venture of the partnership continues to be carried on by any of its partners in a partnership.
A partnership shall terminate when 50 percent or more of the total interest in partnership capital and profits is sold or exchanged within a period of 12 consecutive months.

explanation: Naming revocable beneficiaries of a life insurance policy the taxpayer owns does not transfer dominion and control, so no completed gift occurs. Premiums paid on the taxpayer’s own policy increase the value of property he already owns, and the death proceeds are not lifetime gifts.

quotes.quote: As to any property , or part thereof or interest therein, of which the donor has so parted with dominion and control as to leave in him no power to change its disposition, whether for his own benefit or for the benefit of another, the gift is complete.
A donor purchases from a life insurance company for the benefit of another a life insurance contract or a contract for the payment of an annuity . The value of the gift is the cost of the contract.

explanation: Under § 732(b), the basis of property received in a complete liquidation equals Gulde’s adjusted partnership basis reduced by cash distributed in the same transaction. Thus $26,000 − $12,000 = $14,000; the land’s $10,000 partnership basis and $30,000 FMV do not control here.

quotes.quote: The basis of property (other than money ) distributed by a partnership to a partner in liquidation of the partner’s interest shall be an amount equal to the adjusted basis of such partner’s interest in the partnership reduced by any money distributed in the same transaction.

explanation: Section 57(a)(1) treats only the excess of percentage depletion over the property’s adjusted basis as an AMT tax preference. Long-term capital gain and dividends from publicly-held companies are not listed as tax preference items, so West’s preference amount is $9,000.

quotes.quote: With respect to each property (as defined in section 614), the excess of the deduction for depletion allowable under section 611 for the taxable year over the adjusted basis of the property at the end of the taxable year (determined without regard to the depletion deduction for the taxable year).
increased by the amount of the items of tax preference described in section 57.

explanation: Under IRC § 6075(a), an estate tax return required by § 6018(a) must be filed within 9 months after the decedent’s death. Nine months after May 15, year 2, is February 15, year 3. No extension is assumed, so the return is due on that date.

quotes.quote: Returns made under section 6018(a) (relating to estate taxes) shall be filed within 9 months after the date of the decedent’s death.

explanation: For a tax-shelter position, §6694(a)(2)(C) provides that the position is unreasonable unless the preparer reasonably believed it would more likely than not be sustained on the merits. Disclosure does not reduce the standard to reasonable basis, and substantial authority or a mere reasonable possibility of success is insufficient for a tax shelter.

quotes.quote: If the position is with respect to a tax shelter (as defined in section 6662(d)(2)(C)(ii)) or a reportable transaction to which section 6662A applies, the position is described in this paragraph unless it is reasonable to believe that the position would more likely than not be sustained on its merits.

quotes.quote: gross income does not include interest on any State or local bond

there shall be allowed as a deduction State and local, and foreign, taxes not described in the preceding sentence which are paid or accrued within the taxable year in carrying on a trade or business or an activity described in section 212 (relating to expenses for production of income).

explanation: Because Aston and Becker are equal partners, Aston's distributive share of the partnership's $20,000 ordinary income is $10,000 under §704(a). The $12,000 long-term capital gain is a separately stated item under §702(a)(2), and the $5,000 cash distribution does not reduce ordinary income; since it is below Aston's $40,000 basis, no gain is recognized under §731(a)(1).

quotes.quote: A partner’s distributive share of income, gain, loss, deduction, or credit shall, except as otherwise provided in this chapter, be determined by the partnership agreement.

gain shall not be recognized to such partner, except to the extent that any money distributed exceeds the adjusted basis of such partner’s interest in the partnership immediately before the distribution

explanation: Section 351 generally defers gain on a contribution to a controlled corporation, but § 357(c) treats liabilities assumed (or to which the property is subject) in excess of the transferred property’s adjusted basis as recognized gain. Here, the $12,000 liability exceeds the $6,000 basis by $6,000; the $20,000 fair market value does not change that result.

quotes.quote: if the sum of the amount of the liabilities assumed exceeds the total of the adjusted basis of the property transferred pursuant to such exchange, then such excess shall be considered as a gain from the sale or exchange of a capital asset or of property which is not a capital asset, as the case may be.

if an individual transfers, under section 351, properties having a total basis in his hands of $20,000, one of which has a basis of $10,000 but is subject to a mortgage of $30,000, to a corporation controlled by him, such individual will be subject to tax with respect to $10,000, the excess of the amount of the liability over the total adjusted basis of all the properties in his hands.

explanation: Jackson’s signed promise made a firm offer; because no time was stated, it was irrevocable for a reasonable time, so the later revocation was ineffective. Sands’s mailed acceptance was a reasonable medium and, under the UCC mailbox rule, became effective when mailed on day 7 rather than when received.

quotes.quote: An offer by a merchant to buy or sell goods in a signed writing which by its terms gives assurance that it will be held open is not revocable, for lack of consideration, during the time stated or if no time is stated for a reasonable time, but in no event may such period of irrevocability exceed three months
an offer to make a contract shall be construed as inviting acceptance in any manner and by any medium reasonable in the circumstances

explanation: Sections 6695(a), (b), and (d) expressly penalize a preparer’s failure to furnish a copy to the taxpayer, failure to sign, and failure to retain a copy or list for the required period. Neither those provisions nor sections 6107 and 6694 impose a preparer penalty for failing to notify a taxpayer of an inadvertent error on a return filed 10 years earlier.

quotes.quote: Any person who is a tax return preparer with respect to any return or claim for refund who fails to comply with section 6107(a) with respect to such return or claim shall pay a penalty of $50 for such failure, unless it is shown that such failure is due to reasonable cause and not due to willful neglect.

who is required by regulations prescribed by the Secretary to sign such return or claim, and who fails to comply with such regulations with respect to such return or claim shall pay a penalty of $50 for such failure

explanation: Section 248 permits amortization of qualifying organizational expenditures, but expenditures connected with issuing or selling shares of stock are expressly excluded. Treasury Regulation § 1.248-1(b)(3)(i) treats stock issuance costs as non-organizational expenditures, so they cannot be amortized under section 248.

quotes.quote: The following expenditures are not organizational expenditures within the meaning of section 248 and this section: (i) Expenditures connected with issuing or selling shares of stock or other securities, such as commissions, professional fees, and printing costs.

explanation: Section 6501(a) generally requires assessment within three years after a return is filed, and the fraud exception does not apply because the agent found no fraud. Since the returns were filed on their original due dates, by year 6 the limitations period had expired for several of years 1 through 5, so the multiyear adjustment is improper for those time-barred years.

quotes.quote: Except as otherwise provided in this section, the amount of any tax imposed by this title shall be assessed within 3 years after the return was filed (whether or not such return was filed on or after the date prescribed) or, if the tax is payable by stamp, at any time after such tax became due and before the expiration of 3 years after the date on which any part of such tax was paid, and no proceeding in court without assessment for the collection of such tax shall be begun after the expiration of such period.
In the case of a false or fraudulent return with the intent to evade tax, the tax may be assessed, or a proceeding in court for collection of such tax may be begun without assessment, at any time.

explanation: Under the § 6694 regulations, a preparer generally may rely on client information but must make appropriate inquiries when the Code or regulations require specific facts or documentation as a condition of a deduction. Because business travel expense deductions depend on substantiation, failing to inquire about documentation can expose the CPA to a tax return preparer penalty if the return understates liability; it does not by itself establish fraud or resolve the client’s penalties.

quotes.quote: The tax return preparer must make appropriate inquiries to determine the existence of facts and circumstances required by a Code section or regulation as a condition of the claiming of a deduction or credit .

E did not inquire about the existence of a qualified appraisal or complete a Form 8283, Noncash Charitable Contributions , in accordance with the reporting and substantiation requirements under section 170(f)(11). E reported a deduction on the tax return for the charitable contribution , which resulted in an understatement of liability for tax , and signed the tax return as the tax return preparer . E is subject to a penalty under section 6694.

explanation: Under IRC § 1015(a), the child’s basis for determining gain is the donor’s carryover basis of $40,000, while the basis for determining loss is the $30,000 fair market value at the time of the gift. Because the $36,000 selling price falls between those two bases, no gain or loss is recognized; the regulation’s example is directly analogous.

quotes.quote: except that if such basis (adjusted for the period before the date of the gift as provided in section 1016) is greater than the fair market value of the property at the time of the gift, then for the purpose of determining loss the basis shall be such fair market value.
The basis for determining loss is $90,000; therefore, there is no loss . Furthermore, there is no gain , since the basis for determining gain is $100,000.

explanation: Under LIFO, closing inventory is treated as consisting first of the opening inventory in acquisition order, then current-year acquisitions, so the inventory remaining on hand reflects the earliest acquired goods. The other choices are wrong: LIFO generally raises cost of sales and lowers taxable income when prices rise, annual IRS permission is not required, and the LIFO conformity rule generally requires LIFO for the relevant financial reports.

quotes.quote: Treat those remaining on hand at the close of the taxable year as being: First, those included in the opening inventory of the taxable year (in the order of acquisition) to the extent thereof; and second, those acquired in the taxable year;

Under this last-in, first-out (LIFO) inventory method, the taxpayer is permitted to treat those goods remaining on hand at the close of the taxable year as being: (1) Those included in the opening inventory of the taxable year , in the order of acquisition and to the extent thereof, and (2) Those acquired during the taxable year .

explanation: Greene's beginning basis is increased by the $2,000 of tax-exempt municipal bond interest, because tax-exempt income is an item of income passed through under § 1366(a)(1)(A) and increases S corporation stock basis under § 1367(a)(1). The basis is then reduced by the $5,000 ordinary loss and the $6,000 distribution, yielding $15,000 + $2,000 − $5,000 − $6,000 = $6,000.

explanation: Lemon’s original cost basis was 2,000 × $10.50 = $21,000. The 5% nontaxable stock dividend increased the shares to 2,100, and the later 2-for-1 split increased them to 4,200, without changing total basis; thus each share has $5 of basis, and the 800 shares sold have an $4,000 basis.

determined by allocating between the old stock and the new stock the adjusted basis of the old stock.

the basis of the stock with respect to which the distribution was made shall be allocated between the old and new stocks or rights in proportion to the fair market values of each on the date of distribution

explanation: Under IRC §1015(a), a donee's basis is the donor's carryover basis ($10,000), but where that basis exceeds the fair market value at the date of gift ($9,000), the basis used to determine loss is limited to the $9,000 fair market value. Because the child sold for $7,000 — below the $9,000 gift-date value — the applicable basis (for computing the $2,000 loss) is $9,000; the initial guess of B is therefore correct.

quotes.quote: the basis shall be the same as it would be in the hands of the donor or the last preceding owner by whom it was not acquired by gift, except that if such basis (adjusted for the period before the date of the gift as provided in section 1016) is greater than the fair market value of the property at the time of the gift, then for the purpose of determining loss the basis shall be such fair market value.

explanation: Marketable securities are generally property not specifically excluded by § 1221, so they are typically capital assets. By contrast, inventory is excluded by § 1221(a)(1), depreciable business machinery and equipment by § 1221(a)(2), and ordinary accounts receivable by § 1221(a)(4).

quotes.quote: the term “ capital asset ” means property held by the taxpayer (whether or not connected with his trade or business), but does not include—
The term capital assets includes all classes of property not specifically excluded by section 1221.

explanation: Impossibility of performance is an excuse that can relieve a party of contractual duties by operation of law when an unforeseen event makes performance impossible. Novation and accord and satisfaction are discharge mechanisms based on agreement, while anticipatory repudiation gives the nonbreaching party remedies for breach rather than automatically discharging duties.

quotes.quote: Under contract law, a party can raise an impossibility defense when an unforeseen event occurs after the contract is made which makes performance impossible.

Delay in delivery or non-delivery in whole or in part by a seller who complies with paragraphs (b) and (c) is not a breach of his duty under a contract for sale if performance as agreed has been made impracticable by the occurrence of a contingency the non-occurrence of which was a basic assumption on which the contract was made

explanation: Section 1244 permits a single individual to treat up to $50,000 of loss on qualifying small business stock as an ordinary loss each taxable year. The regulations expressly provide that a prior NOL carryover attributable in part to a section 1244 loss does not reduce the maximum section 1244 ordinary loss allowable in the current year, so Summer may deduct the entire current $50,000 section 1244 loss as ordinary.

quotes.quote: Any amount of loss in excess of the applicable limitation is treated as loss from the sale or exchange of a capital asset.

A taxpayer may deduct the maximum of ordinary loss permitted under section 1244(b) even though all or a portion of the taxpayer 's net operating loss carryback or carryover for the taxable year was, when incurred, a loss on section 1244 stock.
A may deduct the full $50,000 as an ordinary loss under section 1244 and the full $15,000 as a net operating loss carryover in 1981.

explanation: Under 31 C.F.R. § 10.21, a practitioner who knows that a client has made an error in or omission from a return submitted under the revenue laws must advise the client promptly of the error and its consequences. The rule requires prompt advice to the client, not amended-return preparation within 30 days, workpaper documentation, or resignation.

quotes.quote: A practitioner who, having been retained by a client with respect to a matter administered by the Internal Revenue Service , knows that the client has not complied with the revenue laws of the United States or has made an error in or omission from any return, document, affidavit, or other paper which the client submitted or executed under the revenue laws of the United States, must advise the client promptly of the fact of such noncompliance, error, or omission. The practitioner must advise the client of the consequences as provided under the Code and regulations of such noncompliance, error, or omission.

explanation: Distributable net income starts with the trust's taxable income, but capital gains allocated to corpus are excluded unless distributed or treated as distributable. Thus, $2,500 dividends + $2,000 interest − $500 accounting fees − $750 trustee fees = $3,250; the $5,000 capital gain allocated to corpus is excluded.

quotes.quote: Gains from the sale or exchange of capital assets shall be excluded to the extent that such gains are allocated to corpus and are not (A) paid, credited, or required to be distributed to any beneficiary during the taxable year

gains from the sale or exchange of capital assets are ordinarily excluded from distributable net income and are not ordinarily considered as paid , credited, or required to be distributed to any beneficiary.

explanation: A general partner may act as the partnership’s agent and bind it through contracts within actual or apparent authority, so C is not the clearest disqualifier. quotes.quote: Partnerships are composed of partners , who are agents of the partnership and may enter into contracts on behalf of the partnership.

explanation: Assuming the exchange qualifies under §1031, Vinton realizes $120,000 ($550,000 FMV received + $100,000 mortgage relief − $300,000 basis − $230,000 mortgage assumed), but recognizes no gain because the $100,000 liability treated as money received is offset by the $230,000 liability he assumes. then the basis shall be the same as that of the property exchanged, decreased in the amount of any money received by the taxpayer and increased in the amount of gain or decreased in the amount of loss to the taxpayer that was recognized on such exchange.

explanation: Rigg directly owns 85% of Steele, so Rigg and Steele are affiliated. For Urco, Rigg and Steele—both includible corporations in the group—together directly own 90% of Urco (40% + 50%), so Urco also meets the 80% voting-and-value test and all three corporations may file a consolidated return.

quotes.quote: The term “ affiliated group ” means— (A) 1 or more chains of includible corporations connected through stock ownership with a common parent corporation which is an includible corporation , but only if— (B) (i) the common parent owns directly stock meeting the requirements of paragraph (2) in at least 1 of the other includible corporations , and (ii) stock meeting the requirements of paragraph (2) in each of the includible corporations (except the common parent) is owned directly by 1 or more of the other includible corporations .

explanation: Under the traditional agency rule, Frost's adjudicated incompetence terminated Long's non-durable authority by operation of law, regardless of whether Long or Grant had notice. quotes.quote: Typically, a power of attorney only remains effective as long as the principal is alive and competent to make decisions. Principals may, however, grant durable powers of attorney that persist after they are no longer able to make their own decisions.
